Hebrew Bible (the Term)
HEE-broo BY-buhl
noun (academic label)
Hebrew from the language of the patriarchs and prophets; Bible from Greek biblia, books — here the modern academy's preferred label for what Christians call the Old Testament.

📖 Biblical Definition

"Hebrew Bible" is the modern academy's preferred name for the books Christians have always called the Old Testament. It is favored in the university because it appears neutral: it avoids the Christian category "Old," which implies a "New" and a fulfillment in Christ, and it satisfies a setting that wishes to study these books apart from the church's confession. This dictionary explains the term in order to decline it. The label is not innocent; it embodies a judgment — that the Hebrew Scriptures stand on their own, complete in themselves, owned by no covenant community in particular. But the Lord Jesus did not read them so. On the Emmaus road, "beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself" (Luke 24:27). He declared, "they are they which testify of me" (John 5:39). The apostles preached Christ from these very books (Acts 17:2-3). To call them merely the "Hebrew Bible" is to sever them from the One they were written to reveal. This dictionary therefore keeps "Old Testament" — old not as outdated but as the first and foundational covenant fulfilled in the new. The Hebrew Scriptures are Christian Scripture, read rightly only in Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The academy's preferred label for the Old Testament, framed to avoid the Christian category. This dictionary keeps "Old Testament," for the Hebrew Scriptures are Christian Scripture fulfilled in Christ.

HEBREW BIBLE, noun. The modern academic label for the Old Testament, chosen to appear neutral toward Christian and Jewish readings alike.

It avoids the term "Old," which implies fulfillment in a "New" Testament.

"Search the scriptures... they are they which testify of me" (John 5:39).

The label severs the books from the Christ they were written to reveal.

This dictionary keeps "Old Testament," for these are Christian Scripture in Christ.

📖 Key Scripture

Luke 24:27 — "And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself."

John 5:39 — "Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me."

2 Tim 3:15 — "And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus."

Luke 24:44 — "And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The corruption is the academic preference for "Hebrew Bible" over "Old Testament," a label that detaches the Hebrew Scriptures from their fulfillment in Christ.

expand to see more

The term is promoted as scholarly neutrality, but neutrality toward Christ is impossible; to set Him aside is already to take a side. By replacing "Old Testament" with "Hebrew Bible," the academy treats these books as a self-standing artifact of ancient religion rather than as the first volume of the one Christian Scripture. This fits the historical-critical posture, which reads the texts as the late and layered product of Israel's religious development rather than as the inspired and Christ-bearing Word.

The Lord answers the question Himself. He read Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms as concerning Him (Luke 24:44), and rebuked those who searched the Scriptures yet missed their testimony to Him (John 5:39). Paul reasoned with the Jews "out of the scriptures" that Jesus is the Christ (Acts 17:2-3). "Old Testament" confesses this: old as first and foundational, fulfilled and not annulled in the new. This dictionary keeps the historic name and confesses the Hebrew Scriptures to be Christian Scripture, "able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus" (2 Tim 3:15).

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The label joins Hebrew to Bible to name the Old Testament without its Christian frame; this dictionary reads those same books as fulfilled in Christ.
